claim: Immune cells activate in binary, switch-like fashion via large protein assemblies known as signalosomes.
source: Immune cells activate in binary, switch-like fashion via large protein assemblies known as signalosomes, but the molecular mechanism of the switch is not yet understood.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract introducing the context of the study.

claim: The molecular mechanism of the switch in signalosomes is not yet understood.
source: Immune cells activate in binary, switch-like fashion via large protein assemblies known as signalosomes, but the molecular mechanism of the switch is not yet understood.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract indicating a gap in knowledge.

claim: The CBM signalosome governs nuclear transcription factor-κB activation in both innate and adaptive immunity.
source: Here, we employed an in-cell biophysical approach to dissect the assembly mechanism of the CARD-BCL10-MALT1 (CBM) signalosome, which governs nuclear transcription factor-κB activation in both innate and adaptive immunity.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract describing the function of the CBM signalosome.

claim: The switch in the CBM signalosome consists of a sequence-encoded and deeply conserved nucleation barrier to ordered polymerization by the adaptor protein BCL10.
source: We found that the switch consists of a sequence-encoded and deeply conserved nucleation barrier to ordered polymerization by the adaptor protein BCL10.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract.

claim: The particular structure of the BCL10 polymers did not matter for activity.
source: The particular structure of the BCL10 polymers did not matter for activity.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract.

claim: Endogenous BCL10 is functionally supersaturated even in unstimulated human cells.
source: Using optogenetic tools and single-cell transcriptional reporters, we discovered that endogenous BCL10 is functionally supersaturated even in unstimulated human cells, and this results in a predetermined response to stimulation upon nucleation by activated CARD multimers.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract.

claim: Supersaturation of BCL10 results in a predetermined response to stimulation upon nucleation by activated CARD multimers.
source: Using optogenetic tools and single-cell transcriptional reporters, we discovered that endogenous BCL10 is functionally supersaturated even in unstimulated human cells, and this results in a predetermined response to stimulation upon nucleation by activated CARD multimers.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract.

claim: The nucleation barrier in BCL10 is conserved from cnidaria to humans.
source: We found that the nucleation barrier is conserved from cnidaria to humans.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract.

claim: The preassembled CBM signalosome has evolved to store energy analogously to a spring-loaded mousetrap that allows cells to constitutively anticipate and respond to the slightest provocation.
source: Altogether, our work indicates that the preassembled CBM signalosome has evolved to store energy analogously to a spring-loaded mousetrap that allows cells to constitutively anticipate and respond to the slightest provocation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings stated in the abstract.

claim: NF-κB directs the transcription of genes encoding pro-inflammatory cytokines and growth factors that are essential to both innate and adaptive immune responses.
source: NF-κB directs the transcription of genes encoding pro-inflammatory cytokines and growth factors that are essential to both innate and adaptive immune responses, and its improper regulation contributes to cancer, chronic inflammation, and autoimmune diseases.
evidence: This is background knowledge stated in the introduction.

claim: Improper regulation of NF-κB contributes to cancer, chronic inflammation, and autoimmune diseases.
source: NF-κB directs the transcription of genes encoding pro-inflammatory cytokines and growth factors that are essential to both innate and adaptive immune responses, and its improper regulation contributes to cancer, chronic inflammation, and autoimmune diseases.
evidence: This is background knowledge stated in the introduction.

claim: NF-κB responds in switch-like fashion to certain stimuli.
source: Although NF-κB is known to respond in switch-like fashion to certain stimuli (Kingeter et al., 2010; Muñoz et al., 2019; Tay et al., 2010; Figure 1A), the thermodynamic basis of bistability has not been determined.
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The thermodynamic basis of bistability in NF-κB response has not been determined.
source: Although NF-κB is known to respond in switch-like fashion to certain stimuli (Kingeter et al., 2010; Muñoz et al., 2019; Tay et al., 2010; Figure 1A), the thermodynamic basis of bistability has not been determined.
evidence: This is a statement indicating a gap in knowledge.

claim: The CBM signalosome is composed of a CARD-CC family member, BCL10, and MALT1.
source: Named for its three protein constituents, the CBM signalosome is composed of: (1) a Caspase Activation and Recruitment Domain (CARD)-coiled coil (-CC) family member (either CARD9, 10, 11, or 14); (2) B-cell lymphoma 10 (BCL10); and (3) mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma translocation protein 1 (MALT1) (Gehring et al., 2018; Lu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a description of the CBM signalosome components supported by citations.

claim: CARD11 expression in the lymphoid lineage controls B- and T-cell activation upon antigen recognition by B- and T-cell receptors.
source: CARD11 expression in the lymphoid lineage controls B- and T-cell activation upon antigen recognition by B- and T-cell receptors (Egawa et al., 2003; Wang et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: CARD9 expression in the myeloid lineage links the antifungal response of monocytes to fungal carbohydrate detection by C-type lectin receptors.
source: CARD9 expression in the myeloid lineage links the antifungal response of monocytes to fungal carbohydrate detection by C-type lectin receptors (Gross et al., 2006; Hsu et al., 2007; Strasser et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Mutations that relieve the normally autoinhibited state of CARD11 promote lymphoid cell proliferation leading to lymphoma.
source: For instance, mutations that relieve the normally autoinhibited state of CARD11 promote lymphoid cell proliferation leading to lymphoma (Compagno et al., 2009; Lenz et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Several mutations in CARD9 cause familial hypersusceptibility to fungal infections.
source: Several mutations in CARD9 cause familial hypersusceptibility to fungal infections (Glocker et al., 2009; Lanternier et al., 2015; Lanternier et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: CARD10 mutations are associated with risk of primary open angle glaucoma.
source: CARD10 mutations are associated with risk of primary open angle glaucoma (Zhou et al., 2016), while CARD14 gain of function mutations cause psoriasis (Fuchs-Telem et al., 2012; Jordan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: CARD14 gain of function mutations cause psoriasis.
source: CARD10 mutations are associated with risk of primary open angle glaucoma (Zhou et al., 2016), while CARD14 gain of function mutations cause psoriasis (Fuchs-Telem et al., 2012; Jordan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Point mutations and translocations involving BCL10 and MALT1 cause immunodeficiencies, testicular cancer, and lymphomas.
source: Point mutations and translocations involving BCL10 and MALT1 cause immunodeficiencies, testicular cancer, and lymphomas (Juilland and Thome, 2018; Kuper-Hommel et al., 2013; Ruland and Hartjes, 2019).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Signalosome assembly involves homotypic polymerization by protein modules in the death domain (DD), Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR), and RIP homotypic interaction motif (RHIM) families.
source: Signalosome assembly involves homotypic polymerization by protein modules in the death domain (DD), Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR), and RIP homotypic interaction motif (RHIM) families (Nanson et al., 2019; Rodríguez Gama et al., 2021; Wu and Fuxreiter, 2016).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Some signalosome polymers, including those of BCL10, exhibit 'prion-like' self-templating activity in vitro or when overexpressed.
source: Some of these polymers, including those of BCL10, exhibit 'prion-like' self-templating activity in vitro or when overexpressed (Cai et al., 2014; Franklin et al., 2014; Holliday et al., 2019; Hou et al., 2011; Kajava et al., 2014; Latty et al., 2018; Lu et al., 2014; Matyszewski et al., 2018; Mompeán et al., 2018; O'Carroll et al., 2020; Qiao et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Prion-like behavior is made possible by a structurally encoded kinetic barrier to de novo assembly, a process known as 'nucleation'.
source: Prion-like behavior is made possible by a structurally encoded kinetic barrier to de novo assembly, a process known as 'nucleation' (Khan et al., 2018; Rodríguez Gama et al., 2021; Serio et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Nucleation involves a rare thermodynamic fluctuation whereby order spontaneously emerges from disorder.
source: Nucleation involves a rare thermodynamic fluctuation whereby order spontaneously emerges from disorder (Vekilov, 2012).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The percentage of T-Sapphire-positive cells increased in a dose-dependent manner for both HEK293T and THP-1 cells upon stimulation.
source: Using flow cytometry, we found that the percentage of T-Sapphire-positive cells increased in a dose-dependent manner for both HEK293T and THP-1 cells (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is a finding from the flow cytometry experiment shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: The distribution of T-Sapphire fluorescence was bimodal, with cells distributing between nonfluorescent and uniformly fluorescent populations.
source: The distribution of T-Sapphire fluorescence was bimodal, with cells distributing between nonfluorescent and uniformly fluorescent populations.
evidence: This is a finding from the flow cytometry experiment.

claim: Increasing doses of stimulation increased the fraction of cells in the fluorescent population, but did not influence the level of fluorescence within that population.
source: Increasing doses increased the fraction of cells in the fluorescent population, but did not influence the level of fluorescence within that population, even across multiple stimulation concentrations spanning several orders of magnitude (Figure 1B,C insets and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This is a finding from the flow cytometry experiment shown in Figure 1B,C and supplementary figures.

claim: Cells lacking BCL10 failed to respond to stimulation.
source: As expected, cells lacking BCL10 failed to respond to stimulation (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is a finding from the flow cytometry experiment shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: CARD9 ran as an oligomer that, upon stimulation, shifted uniformly to a higher molecular weight.
source: We found that CARD9 (62 kDa) ran as an oligomer that, upon stimulation, shifted uniformly to a higher molecular weight (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a finding from the size exclusion chromatography experiment shown in Figure 1F.

claim: BCL10 populated a large (>500 kDa) complex upon stimulation, with a bimodal size distribution.
source: BCL10 (26 kDa) also populated a large (>500 kDa) complex upon stimulation, although in this case, the size distribution was bimodal, with a fraction of the protein remaining monomeric.
evidence: This is a finding from the size exclusion chromatography experiment.

claim: The bimodal size distribution of BCL10 suggests an underlying phase transition.
source: Because the protein does not populate intermediate-sized species, this result suggests an underlying phase transition.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the size exclusion chromatography data.

claim: WT BCL10 formed puncta in 70% of cells treated with β-glucan.
source: Conversely, in cells treated with β-glucan, the WT protein formed puncta in 70% of cells (Figure 1E), while the E53R mutant protein remained dispersed.
evidence: This is a finding from the microscopy experiment shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The E53R mutant of BCL10 remained dispersed even after β-glucan treatment.
source: Conversely, in cells treated with β-glucan, the WT protein formed puncta in 70% of cells (Figure 1E), while the E53R mutant protein remained dispersed.
evidence: This is a finding from the microscopy experiment shown in Figure 1E.

claim: β-glucan-induced p65 nuclear translocation for cells reconstituted with WT, but not E53R mutant, BCL10-mEos3.2.
source: We found that β-glucan-induced p65 nuclear translocation for cells reconstituted with WT, but not E53R mutant, BCL10-mEos3.2.
evidence: This is a finding from the immunostaining experiment.

claim: The degree of p65 nuclear translocation in the reconstituted cells resembled that of WT THP-1 cells treated with β-glucan.
source: Moreover, the degree of p65 nuclear translocation in the reconstituted cells resembled that of WT THP-1 cells treated with β-glucan (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: This is a finding from the immunostaining experiment shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, B.

claim: The CBM signalosome exerts binary control over NF-κB activation in monocytes.
source: Together, these results suggest that the CBM signalosome exerts binary control over NF-κB activation in monocytes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: CARD9 formed low AmFRET multimers across the full range of concentrations.
source: We found that neither CARD9 nor MALT1 formed self-templating polymers. The former formed low AmFRET multimers across the full range of concentrations (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 2B.

claim: CARD9 accumulated into a single irregular punctum in each cell.
source: These corresponded to the protein's accumulation into a single irregular punctum in each cell (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the imaging flow cytometry experiment shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: There was no discontinuity in DAmFRET for CARD9 and hence no observable nucleation barrier to the formation of puncta at the cellular level.
source: There was no discontinuity in DAmFRET and hence no observable nucleation barrier to the formation of these puncta at the cellular level.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DAmFRET data for CARD9.

claim: MALT1 remained completely monomeric.
source: MALT1 remained completely monomeric (Figure 3D, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 3D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: BCL10 produced a clear bimodal distribution wherein cells partitioned between a no-AmFRET population and a high-AmFRET population.
source: BCL10, in contrast, produced a clear bimodal distribution wherein cells partitioned between a no-AmFRET population and a high-AmFRET population, respectively, comprised of cells containing only monomeric BCL10 or highly polymerized BCL10 (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The two populations of BCL10 overlapped in their expression levels, indicating that BCL10 can accumulate to supersaturating concentrations while remaining monomeric.
source: The two populations overlapped in their expression levels, indicating that BCL10 can accumulate to supersaturating concentrations while remaining monomeric, but then polymerizes following a stochastic nucleation event.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DAmFRET data for BCL10.

claim: The paucity of cells between the two populations of BCL10 suggests that BCL10 polymerizes rapidly to a new steady state following a single nucleation event in each cell.
source: The paucity of cells between the two populations, that is with moderate levels of AmFRET, suggests that BCL10 polymerizes rapidly to a new steady state following a single nucleation event in each cell (Khan et al., 2018; Posey et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DAmFRET data for BCL10 supported by citations.

claim: MALT1DD remained monomeric at all concentrations.
source: MALT1DD remained monomeric at all concentrations (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: CARD9CARD was monomeric up to a threshold concentration of approximately 100 µM, above which it readily polymerized with only a slight discontinuity.
source: CARD9CARD was monomeric up to a threshold concentration of approximately 100 µM, above which it readily polymerized with only a slight discontinuity (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: BCL10CARD switched from monomer to polymer with a large discontinuity resembling that of FL BCL10.
source: In contrast, BCL10CARD switched from monomer to polymer with a large discontinuity (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E) resembling that of FL BCL10, suggesting that the large nucleation barrier of the FL protein, and by extension the switch-like assembly of the CBM assembly, can be attributed to the CARD of BCL10.
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The large nucleation barrier of the FL BCL10 protein, and by extension the switch-like assembly of the CBM assembly, can be attributed to the CARD of BCL10.
source: In contrast, BCL10CARD switched from monomer to polymer with a large discontinuity (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E) resembling that of FL BCL10, suggesting that the large nucleation barrier of the FL protein, and by extension the switch-like assembly of the CBM assembly, can be attributed to the CARD of BCL10.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DAmFRET data.

claim: BCL10CARD undergoes a greater conformational change to polymerize than does either CARD9CARD or MALT1DD.
source: By computationally superposing the structures of the monomer and polymer forms for each domain, and calculating the root mean square deviation (RMSD) between backbone C-alpha atoms, we found that BCL10CARD undergoes a greater conformational change to polymerize than does either CARD9CARD or MALT1DD (Figure 2E–G; RMSD 3.581, 1.655, and 0.956 Å, respectively).
evidence: This is a finding from the structural analysis shown in Figure 2E–G.

claim: The greater conformational change in BCL10CARD is consistent with the nucleation barrier of BCL10CARD resulting from a particularly unfavorable conformational fluctuation.
source: Although more sophisticated analyses are required to relate these differences to nucleation barriers, they are consistent with the nucleation barrier of BCL10CARD resulting from a particularly unfavorable conformational fluctuation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural analysis data.

claim: The R58G mutation of BCL10 was first described in a germ cell line tumor and shown to hyperactivate NF-κB.
source: The R58G mutation of BCL10 was first described in a germ cell line tumor and shown to hyperactivate NF-κB (Willis et al., 1999).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The R58G mutation reduced both ẟ and EC50 relative to WT BCL10.
source: Indeed, relative to WT, R58G reduced both ẟ and EC50 (Figure 2H,I).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 2H,I.

claim: The R36E mutation increased both ẟ and EC50 relative to WT BCL10.
source: In contrast, mutation R36E, which disrupts polymer interface IIa (David et al., 2018), increased both ẟ and EC50 (Figure 2I).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 2I.

claim: The E53R mutant blocked nucleation at all tested concentrations.
source: Consistent with previous observations, mutant E53R, which disrupts polymer interface IIIb (David et al., 2018), blocked nucleation at all tested concentrations (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Position 58 in BCL10 is an arginine in mammals but a glutamine in lamprey, cartilaginous fish, and amphibians.
source: We found via multiple sequence alignment that position 58 is an arginine in mammals but a glutamine in lamprey, cartilaginous fish, and amphibians (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from the multiple sequence alignment shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: R58Q resembled WT BCL10, whereas R58L lowered the nucleation barrier.
source: As expected, R58Q resembled WT, whereas R58L lowered the nucleation barrier (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B, C).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B, C.

claim: Arg or Gln residues at position 58 functionally oppose nucleation and thereby prevent precocious activation of BCL10 in the germ cell lineage.
source: These data suggest that Arg or Gln residues at position 58 functionally oppose nucleation and thereby prevent precocious activation of BCL10 in the germ cell lineage.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DAmFRET data.

claim: The native monomeric structure of BCL10 creates a physiological nucleation barrier that allows for switch-like self-assembly and all-or-none NF-κB activation.
source: Altogether, we conclude that the native monomeric structure of BCL10 creates a physiological nucleation barrier that allows for switch-like self-assembly and all-or-none NF-κB activation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: CARD-CC proteins form oligomers that promote BCL10 polymerization.
source: CARD-CC proteins form oligomers that promote BCL10 polymerization (David et al., 2018; Holliday et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: CARD-CC proteins are believed to reside in an oligomeric state even in the absence of stimulation.
source: Somewhat paradoxically, however, CARD-CC proteins are believed to reside in an oligomeric state even in the absence of stimulation.
evidence: This is a statement of prior knowledge.

claim: The active configuration of CARD-CC proteins is prevented from forming within oligomers due to an inhibitory interaction between the CARD and the adjacent coiled-coil region.
source: The active configuration is prevented from forming within these oligomers due to an inhibitory interaction between the CARD and the adjacent coiled-coil region (Holliday et al., 2019; Sommer et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The inhibitory interaction between the CARD and the adjacent coiled-coil region is released by post-translational modifications induced by pathway activation, leading to CBM assembly.
source: That interaction is released by post-translational modifications induced by pathway activation, leading to CBM assembly.
evidence: This is a statement of prior knowledge.

claim: FL CARD9 forms a punctum at all expression levels, whereas the CARD itself forms either monomers (at low expression) or polymers (at high expression).
source: Our observation that FL CARD9 forms a punctum at all expression levels, whereas the CARD itself forms either monomers (at low expression) or polymers (at high expression), is consistent with an essential role of non-CARD interactions in both autoinhibition and higher-order assembly.
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiments.

claim: Non-CARD interactions play an essential role in both autoinhibition and higher-order assembly of CARD9.
source: Our observation that FL CARD9 forms a punctum at all expression levels, whereas the CARD itself forms either monomers (at low expression) or polymers (at high expression), is consistent with an essential role of non-CARD interactions in both autoinhibition and higher-order assembly.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DAmFRET data.

claim: CARD9 lacking its CARD aggregated just as robustly as FL CARD9.
source: Remarkably, this truncated protein aggregated just as robustly as FL (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C), suggesting that coiled-coil interactions are predominantly if not entirely responsible for its multimerization in the inactive state.
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: Coiled-coil interactions are predominantly if not entirely responsible for CARD9 multimerization in the inactive state.
source: Remarkably, this truncated protein aggregated just as robustly as FL (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C), suggesting that coiled-coil interactions are predominantly if not entirely responsible for its multimerization in the inactive state.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DAmFRET data.

claim: CARD9 1-142 multimerized at all concentrations.
source: We found that even the shortest variant tested (1–142), retaining only 44 residues of additional sequence beyond the CARD, multimerized at all concentrations (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: CARD9 1-142 populated a lower AmFRET state and exclusively soluble oligomers, consistent with the reduced valency of the truncated coiled-coil region.
source: Unlike longer versions of the protein, however, this variant populated a lower AmFRET state and exclusively soluble oligomers, consistent with the reduced valency of the truncated coiled-coil region (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: None of the CARD9 truncation constructs formed the higher AmFRET state or fibrillar puncta that would be indicative of polymerization.
source: Importantly, none of these constructs formed the higher AmFRET state or fibrillar puncta that would be indicative of polymerization.
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiments.

claim: The tight relationship between multimerization and inhibition can be rationalized by the previously solved structure of the autoinhibited dimer formed by the short variant, wherein each CARD packs against the broad face of the immediately adjacent dimeric coiled-coil, making extensive contacts with both helices.
source: This tight relationship between multimerization and inhibition can be rationalized by the previously solved structure of the autoinhibited dimer formed by the short variant, wherein each CARD packs against the broad face of the immediately adjacent dimeric coiled-coil, making extensive contacts with both helices (Holliday et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The mutant I107E achieved higher AmFRET at low expression and rendered the punctum less spherical relative to WT CARD9.
source: Relative to WT, the mutant I107E achieved higher AmFRET at low expression and rendered the punctum less spherical (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, F.

claim: Multimerization itself is not inhibitory to nucleation and once autoinhibition is released, CARD–CARD interactions stabilize the aggregated state.
source: Together with the prior demonstration of functional activity, the present findings suggest that multimerization itself is not inhibitory to nucleation and that once autoinhibition is released, CARD–CARD interactions stabilize the aggregated state.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data.

claim: Pre-multimerization driven by the multivalent coiled-coil expedites the response to stimulation, perhaps by allowing stimulus-dependent post-translational modifications to occur cooperatively on multiple CARD9 subunits in close proximity.
source: We therefore speculate that pre-multimerization driven by the multivalent coiled-coil expedites the response to stimulation, perhaps by allowing stimulus-dependent post-translational modifications (Zhong et al., 2018) to occur cooperatively on multiple CARD9 subunits in close proximity.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the data and supported by a citation.

claim: High expression levels of CARD9CARD-mCardinal sufficed to nucleate BCL10-mEos3.1, whereas mCardinal itself had no such activity.
source: We noticed that high expression levels of CARD9CARD-mCardinal sufficed to nucleate BCL10-mEos3.1, whereas mCardinal itself had no such activity (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,C), suggesting that polymers of CARD9CARD itself can nucleate BCL10.
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,C.

claim: Polymers of CARD9CARD itself can nucleate BCL10.
source: We noticed that high expression levels of CARD9CARD-mCardinal sufficed to nucleate BCL10-mEos3.1, whereas mCardinal itself had no such activity (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,C), suggesting that polymers of CARD9CARD itself can nucleate BCL10.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DAmFRET data.

claim: CARD9CARD-μNS-mCardinal shifted all BCL10-mEos3.1 yeast cells to the high-FRET population.
source: As hypothesized, CARD9CARD-μNS-mCardinal shifted all BCL10-mEos3.1 yeast cells to the high-FRET population (Figure 3B), confirming that CARD9CARD indeed forms a polymer seed when condensed.
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 3B.

claim: CARD9CARD indeed forms a polymer seed when condensed.
source: As hypothesized, CARD9CARD-μNS-mCardinal shifted all BCL10-mEos3.1 yeast cells to the high-FRET population (Figure 3B), confirming that CARD9CARD indeed forms a polymer seed when condensed.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DAmFRET data.

claim: In the absence of a template, BCL10 is supersaturated even at the lowest levels of expression (nanomolar).
source: Moreover, the data indicate that in the absence of a template, BCL10 is supersaturated even at the lowest levels of expression (nanomolar).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DAmFRET data.

claim: CARD9CARD-μNS-mCardinal had no effect on the DAmFRET profile of CARD9CARD-mEos3.1, suggesting that CARD9CARD instead forms labile polymers with no observable nucleation barrier at the cellular level.
source: In striking contrast, CARD9CARD-μNS-mCardinal had no effect on the DAmFRET profile of CARD9CARD-mEos3.1, suggesting that CARD9CARD instead forms labile polymers with no observable nucleation barrier at the cellular level (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 3B.

claim: All CARD-CC family members (CARD10, 11, and 14) polymerized comparably to that of CARD9.
source: We performed DAmFRET on their CARD and found that all polymerized comparably to that of CARD9 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E), that is only at high concentrations (the most stable polymers were formed by CARD10, but even then only above approximately 40 µM), and with negligible nucleation barriers.
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E.

claim: All CARD-CC family members, when artificially condensed by fusion to μNS-mCardinal, suffice to nucleate BCL10.
source: We then asked if they too, when artificially condensed by fusion to μNS-mCardinal, suffice to nucleate BCL10. Indeed all exhibited this activity (Figure 3—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2F.

claim: All four CARD-CC proteins share a common mechanism of action.
source: These findings suggest a shared mechanism of action by all four CARD-CC proteins.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DAmFRET data.

claim: The pathogenic mutants R18W, R35Q, R57H, and G72S of CARD9CARD failed to form polymers.
source: Whereas WT CARD9CARD assembled into polymers at high concentration, the pathogenic mutants R18W, R35Q, R57H, and G72S failed to do so (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 3B, C).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 3B, C.

claim: The R70W mutant of CARD9CARD not only retained the ability to polymerize, but did so at lower concentrations than WT.
source: Remarkably, however, the R70W mutant not only retained the ability to polymerize, but did so at lower concentrations than WT (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 3B, C), implying that its defect instead lies downstream of multimerization.
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 3B, C.

claim: The defect of the R70W mutant lies downstream of multimerization.
source: Remarkably, however, the R70W mutant not only retained the ability to polymerize, but did so at lower concentrations than WT (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 3B, C), implying that its defect instead lies downstream of multimerization.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the DAmFRET data.

claim: CARD9CARD WT nucleated BCL10-mEos3.1 at all expression levels.
source: As expected CARD9CARD WT nucleated BCL10-mEos3.1 at all expression levels.
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment.

claim: BCL10-mEos3.1 filaments emanated directly from the CARD9CARD-μNS-mCardinal puncta.
source: Using confocal fluorescence microscopy, we observed the BCL10-mEos3.1 filaments emanating directly from the CARD9CARD-μNS-mCardinal puncta.
evidence: This is a finding from the confocal fluorescence microscopy experiment.

claim: None of the pathogenic mutants of CARD9CARD induced BCL10-mEos3.1 nucleation nor observable filaments.
source: In contrast, none of the pathogenic mutants induced BCL10-mEos3.1 nucleation nor observable filaments (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: This is a finding from the confocal fluorescence microscopy experiment shown in Figure 3E,F.

claim: R18W, R35Q, R57H, and G72S are structurally incompatible with the polymeric configuration of CARD9.
source: Collectively, these data reveal that R18W, R35Q, R57H, and G72S are structurally incompatible with the polymeric configuration, whereas R70W specifically disrupts the interaction of CARD9 polymers with BCL10 at interface IIb (Figure 3—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3E.

claim: R70W specifically disrupts the interaction of CARD9 polymers with BCL10 at interface IIb.
source: Collectively, these data reveal that R18W, R35Q, R57H, and G72S are structurally incompatible with the polymeric configuration, whereas R70W specifically disrupts the interaction of CARD9 polymers with BCL10 at interface IIb (Figure 3—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3E.

claim: CARD9 I107E strongly activated NF-κB.
source: We first confirmed that CARD9 I107E strongly activated NF-κB, and that a construct lacking the CARD did not (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from the NF-κB reporter assay shown in Figure 3D.

claim: A CARD9 construct lacking the CARD did not activate NF-κB.
source: We first confirmed that CARD9 I107E strongly activated NF-κB, and that a construct lacking the CARD did not (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from the NF-κB reporter assay shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Every one of the pathogenic mutants of CARD9 eliminated the protein's ability to activate NF-κB.
source: We next introduced each of the pathogenic mutants into this construct and found that every one of them eliminated the protein's ability to activate NF-κB (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from the NF-κB reporter assay shown in Figure 3D.

claim: CARD9 and its orthologs function to nucleate BCL10 by forming a polymeric structure stabilized by multivalent coiled-coil interactions.
source: Altogether, these results suggest that CARD9 and its orthologs function to nucleate BCL10 by forming a polymeric structure stabilized by multivalent coiled-coil interactions, and that disrupting that activity compromises innate immunity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Disrupting the activity of CARD9 to nucleate BCL10 compromises innate immunity.
source: Altogether, these results suggest that CARD9 and its orthologs function to nucleate BCL10 by forming a polymeric structure stabilized by multivalent coiled-coil interactions, and that disrupting that activity compromises innate immunity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: All of the CBM signalosome proteins behaved the same way in HEK293T cells as they did in yeast.
source: Using DAmFRET, we confirmed that all of the proteins behaved the same way in HEK293T cells as they did in yeast.
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiments in HEK293T cells.

claim: FL CARD9 formed irregular higher-order assemblies at all concentrations in HEK293T cells.
source: Specifically, FL CARD9 formed irregular higher-order assemblies at all concentrations (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,C); CARD9CARD polymerized only above a high threshold expression level; MALT1 was entirely monomeric (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A); and BCL10 became supersaturated with respect to a polymerized form (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,C.

claim: CARD9CARD polymerized only above a high threshold expression level in HEK293T cells.
source: Specifically, FL CARD9 formed irregular higher-order assemblies at all concentrations (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,C); CARD9CARD polymerized only above a high threshold expression level; MALT1 was entirely monomeric (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A); and BCL10 became supersaturated with respect to a polymerized form (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiments in HEK293T cells.

claim: MALT1 was entirely monomeric in HEK293T cells.
source: Specifically, FL CARD9 formed irregular higher-order assemblies at all concentrations (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,C); CARD9CARD polymerized only above a high threshold expression level; MALT1 was entirely monomeric (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A); and BCL10 became supersaturated with respect to a polymerized form (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: BCL10 became supersaturated with respect to a polymerized form in HEK293T cells.
source: Specifically, FL CARD9 formed irregular higher-order assemblies at all concentrations (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,C); CARD9CARD polymerized only above a high threshold expression level; MALT1 was entirely monomeric (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A); and BCL10 became supersaturated with respect to a polymerized form (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Neither CARD9 nor MALT1 expression activated NF-κB in HEK293T cells.
source: Neither CARD9 nor MALT1 expression activated NF-κB (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is a finding from the NF-κB reporter assay shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: BCL10 expression robustly activated NF-κB in HEK293T cells.
source: BCL10 expression, in contrast, robustly activated NF-κB (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a finding from the NF-κB reporter assay shown in Figure 4C.

claim: NF-κB activation only occurred in cells that contained BCL10 polymers, and not monomers, irrespective of the expression level of BCL10.
source: Importantly, this activation only occurred in cells that contained BCL10 polymers, and not monomers, irrespective of the expression level of BCL10 (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: This is a finding from the NF-κB reporter assay shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, E.

claim: The frequency of activation, but not the level of activation within individual cells, was reduced or eliminated for the polymer-inhibiting mutants R36E and E53R, respectively.
source: The frequency of activation, but not the level of activation within individual cells, was reduced or eliminated for the polymer-inhibiting mutants R36E and E53R, respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: This is a finding from the NF-κB reporter assay shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, E.

claim: Mutant R58G increased the fraction of cells with activated NF-κB.
source: Mutant R58G increased the fraction of cells with activated NF-κB (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C), as expected from its reduced nucleation barrier.
evidence: This is a finding from the NF-κB reporter assay shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: The intensity of NF-κB response at the cellular level did not differ between the BCL10 mutants.
source: Importantly, the intensity of NF-κB response at the cellular level did not differ between the mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C), suggesting a specific effect on nucleation and not downstream signaling.
evidence: This is a finding from the NF-κB reporter assay shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: The consistent intensity of NF-κB response across BCL10 mutants suggests a specific effect on nucleation and not downstream signaling.
source: Importantly, the intensity of NF-κB response at the cellular level did not differ between the mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C), suggesting a specific effect on nucleation and not downstream signaling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the NF-κB reporter assay data.

claim: ASC formed prion-like polymers.
source: As expected (Cai et al., 2014), ASC formed prion-like polymers (Figure 4B), but did not activate the NF-κB reporter (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 4B, supported by a citation.

claim: ASC did not activate the NF-κB reporter.
source: As expected (Cai et al., 2014), ASC formed prion-like polymers (Figure 4B), but did not activate the NF-κB reporter (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a finding from the NF-κB reporter assay shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Polymers of BCL10, specifically, and independently of upstream components or physiological stimuli, suffice to activate downstream components of the pathway.
source: This experiment suggests that polymers of BCL10, specifically, and independently of upstream components or physiological stimuli, suffice to activate downstream components of the pathway, and that an intrinsic nucleation barrier to their formation causes activation to occur in a binary fashion.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: An intrinsic nucleation barrier to BCL10 polymer formation causes activation to occur in a binary fashion.
source: This experiment suggests that polymers of BCL10, specifically, and independently of upstream components or physiological stimuli, suffice to activate downstream components of the pathway, and that an intrinsic nucleation barrier to their formation causes activation to occur in a binary fashion.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: BCL10 became punctate within 50 min after PMA addition.
source: BCL10 became punctate within 50 min after PMA addition, and the puncta could be observed to elongate with time (Figure 4D,E and Video 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the time-lapse microscopy experiment shown in Figure 4D,E and Video 1.

claim: Concomitantly with BCL10 puncta formation, p65 was observed to translocate to the nucleus.
source: Concomitantly, p65 was observed to translocate to the nucleus (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a finding from the time-lapse microscopy experiment shown in Figure 4E.

claim: BCL10 is supersaturated prior to stimulation.
source: This result suggests that BCL10 is indeed supersaturated prior to stimulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the time-lapse microscopy experiment.

claim: EYFP-p65 failed to translocate to the nucleus in cells with BCL10-mScarlet intensity below an apparent threshold.
source: As expected, EYFP-p65 failed to translocate to the nucleus in cells with BCL10-mScarlet intensity below an apparent threshold (Figure 4—figure supplement 4A, B).
evidence: This is a finding from the confocal microscopy experiment shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4A, B.

claim: By 24 hr of doxycycline induction, a small fraction of cells (1.1%) had spontaneously acquired BCL10 puncta.
source: By 24 hr of doxycycline induction, a small fraction of cells (1.1%) had spontaneously acquired BCL10 puncta. This fraction increased to 5.1% at 48 hr and 7.8% at 72 hr (Figure 4—figure supplement 4C, D).
evidence: This is a finding from the confocal microscopy experiment shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4C, D.

claim: The fraction of cells with spontaneous BCL10 puncta increased to 5.1% at 48 hr and 7.8% at 72 hr of doxycycline induction.
source: By 24 hr of doxycycline induction, a small fraction of cells (1.1%) had spontaneously acquired BCL10 puncta. This fraction increased to 5.1% at 48 hr and 7.8% at 72 hr (Figure 4—figure supplement 4C, D).
evidence: This is a finding from the confocal microscopy experiment shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4C, D.

claim: Cells containing BCL10 puncta also showed EYFP-p65 translocation.
source: As expected, the cells containing BCL10 puncta also showed EYFP-p65 translocation (Figure 4—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This is a finding from the confocal microscopy experiment shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4C.

claim: BCL10 supersaturation is necessary to activate NF-κB, while deep supersaturation is sufficient.
source: We conclude that BCL10 supersaturation is necessary to activate NF-κB, while deep supersaturation is sufficient.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Following a blue light pulse, both CARD9CARD-Cry2 and BCL10-mScarlet assembled into puncta.
source: Following the pulse, however, both proteins assembled into puncta.
evidence: This is a finding from the optogenetic experiment.

claim: CARD9CARD clustering peaked at approximately 5-min post-excitation, and then those clusters disassembled to background levels by approximately 20 min.
source: By measuring the kinetics of CARD9CARD and BCL10 assembly (as the coefficient of variation in pixel intensity over time), we found that CARD9CARD clustering peaked at approximately 5-min post-excitation, and then those clusters disassembled to background levels by approximately 20 min (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a finding from the optogenetic experiment shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Within 6 min following the blue light pulse, BCL10 began to form filamentous puncta that initially colocalized with those of CARD9CARD.
source: Within 6 min following the pulse, BCL10 began to form filamentous puncta that initially colocalized with those of CARD9CARD (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a finding from the optogenetic experiment shown in Figure 5B.

claim: BCL10 puncta continued to elongate even after the CARD9CARD clusters had dissolved.
source: Remarkably, the puncta continued to elongate even after the CARD9CARD clusters had dissolved (Figure 5B and inset), revealing that BCL10 is driven toward a polymeric steady state even in the absence of CARD9 templates.
evidence: This is a finding from the optogenetic experiment shown in Figure 5B.

claim: BCL10 is driven toward a polymeric steady state even in the absence of CARD9 templates.
source: Remarkably, the puncta continued to elongate even after the CARD9CARD clusters had dissolved (Figure 5B and inset), revealing that BCL10 is driven toward a polymeric steady state even in the absence of CARD9 templates.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the optogenetic experiment data.

claim: BCL10 did not polymerize with the R18W and R70W mutants of CARD9CARD-Cry2 despite comparable kinetics of CARD9CARD-Cry2 clustering.
source: To test the specificity of the CARD9-BCL10 interaction, we also performed the experiment with the R18W and R70W mutants of CARD9CARD-Cry2, whereupon BCL10 did not polymerize despite comparable kinetics of CARD9CARD-Cry2 clustering (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This is a finding from the optogenetic experiment shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: Blue light-induced EYFP-p65 to translocate comparably to stimulation with PMA.
source: We observed that blue light-induced EYFP-p65 to translocate comparably to stimulation with PMA (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This is a finding from the optogenetic experiment shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: The degree of p65 translocation within cells did not depend on the duration of the blue light pulse.
source: Additionally, as with the different doses of PMA, the degree of translocation within cells did not depend on the duration of the blue light pulse.
evidence: This is a finding from the optogenetic experiment.

claim: The all-or-none nature of signaling from BCL10 is highlighted by the fact that the degree of translocation within cells did not depend on the duration of the blue light pulse.
source: This again highlights the all-or-none nature of signaling from BCL10.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the optogenetic experiment data.

claim: The polymerization-incompetent mutant of BCL10, E53R, failed to form puncta or activate NF-κB in response to blue light.
source: We found that the polymerization-incompetent mutant of BCL10, E53R, failed to form puncta or activate NF-κB in response to blue light (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is a finding from the optogenetic experiment shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: BCL10 is endogenously supersaturated and physiologically restrained from activation by the kinetic barrier associated with polymer nucleation.
source: Altogether these data indicate that BCL10 is endogenously supersaturated and physiologically restrained from activation by the kinetic barrier associated with polymer nucleation, which collectively allow for switch-like CBM signalosome formation and NF-κB activation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: 25–30% of cells failed to respond to stimulation even at saturating levels of β-glucan or PMA.
source: Throughout our experiments with both THP-1 and HEK293T cells – whether analyzing BCL10 puncta formation, NF-κB transcriptional activity, or p65 translocation – we observed that 25–30% of cells failed to respond to stimulation even at saturating levels of β-glucan or PMA (Figure 1B,C,E and Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a finding from multiple experiments shown in Figure 1B,C,E and Figure 4E.

claim: The size of the recalcitrant population did not depend on whether BCL10 was endogenously or exogenously expressed.
source: The size of this population did not depend on whether BCL10 was endogenously or exogenously expressed, and dropped to 10% in our optogenetic experiments that bypassed upstream factors (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E), together suggesting that recalcitrance results at least in part from an increase in the BCL10 nucleation barrier due to cell-to-cell heterogeneity in upstream factors.
evidence: This is a finding from the experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The recalcitrant population dropped to 10% in optogenetic experiments that bypassed upstream factors.
source: The size of this population did not depend on whether BCL10 was endogenously or exogenously expressed, and dropped to 10% in our optogenetic experiments that bypassed upstream factors (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E), together suggesting that recalcitrance results at least in part from an increase in the BCL10 nucleation barrier due to cell-to-cell heterogeneity in upstream factors.
evidence: This is a finding from the optogenetic experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Recalcitrance results at least in part from an increase in the BCL10 nucleation barrier due to cell-to-cell heterogeneity in upstream factors.
source: The size of this population did not depend on whether BCL10 was endogenously or exogenously expressed, and dropped to 10% in our optogenetic experiments that bypassed upstream factors (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E), together suggesting that recalcitrance results at least in part from an increase in the BCL10 nucleation barrier due to cell-to-cell heterogeneity in upstream factors.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Cells may regulate their sensitivity to stimulation by raising or lowering the nucleation barrier.
source: While the origin of this phenomenon remains to be determined, it demonstrates that cells may regulate their sensitivity to stimulation by raising or lowering the nucleation barrier.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The dimerizing module VfAU1-LOV failed to induce nuclear translocation of p65 when fused to MALT1126-824.
source: When expressed in HEK293T cells containing EYFP-p65 and illuminated with blue light, the dimerizing module failed to induce nuclear translocation, while the multimerizing module did so robustly, and to the same levels as had been achieved for BCL10-mediated activation using HEK293T WT treated with PMA (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a finding from the optogenetic experiment shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The multimerizing module Cry2clust induced robust nuclear translocation of p65 when fused to MALT1126-824.
source: When expressed in HEK293T cells containing EYFP-p65 and illuminated with blue light, the dimerizing module failed to induce nuclear translocation, while the multimerizing module did so robustly, and to the same levels as had been achieved for BCL10-mediated activation using HEK293T WT treated with PMA (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a finding from the optogenetic experiment shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Both VfAU1-LOV and Cry2clust fused to CASP8180-479 triggered rampant cell death upon blue light illumination.
source: As a control that the constructs were each functioning as intended, we also performed experiments with the analogous region of CASP8 (180–479) fused to either VfAU1-LOV or Cry2clust. CASP8 has previously been shown to activate upon dimerization (Demarco et al., 2020). Indeed, both constructs triggered rampant cell death upon blue light illumination (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is a finding from the optogenetic experiment shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B, supported by a citation.

claim: MALT1 is activated by proximity rather than structural order of the adaptor protein polymers.
source: Together these results reveal that MALT1 is activated by proximity rather than structural order of the adaptor protein polymers, consistent with BCL10 having a kinetic rather than a specific structural function.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the optogenetic experiments.

claim: BCL10 has a kinetic rather than a specific structural function.
source: Together these results reveal that MALT1 is activated by proximity rather than structural order of the adaptor protein polymers, consistent with BCL10 having a kinetic rather than a specific structural function.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the optogenetic experiments.

claim: The fact that MALT1 activation requires higher-order multimerization rather than just dimerization may relate to its function in concentrating the ubiquitin ligase TRAF6.
source: The fact that MALT1 activation requires higher-order multimerization rather than just dimerization may relate to its function in concentrating the ubiquitin ligase TRAF6, a critical intermediary in the activation of NF-κB (Ginster et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the data and supported by a citation.

claim: The intensity of T-Sapphire fluorescence increased in a monotonic fashion with the duration of blue light stimulation when MALT1 was activated optogenetically.
source: As expected, the intensity of T-Sapphire fluorescence increased in a monotonic fashion with the duration of blue light stimulation (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: This is a finding from the optogenetic experiment shown in Figure 6E,F.

claim: When cells expressing optogenetic MALT1 were treated with PMA, the NF-κB reporter did not activate.
source: When we instead treated these cells with PMA, the NF-κB reporter did not activate (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a finding from the optogenetic experiment shown in Figure 6E.

claim: BCL10 polymers formed upon PMA treatment are unable to activate MALT1 when it lacks its DD.
source: This result indicates that BCL10 polymers formed upon PMA treatment are unable to activate MALT1 when it lacks its DD, ruling out any unanticipated role of the polymers in structuring MALT1126-824.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the optogenetic experiment data.

claim: BCL10 confers the switch-like activation of NF-κB in WT cells upon physiological CBM stimulation.
source: These data are consistent with BCL10 conferring the switch-like activation of NF-κB in WT cells upon physiological CBM stimulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the optogenetic experiments.

claim: The CBM signalosome originated in the ancient ancestor of cnidarians and bilaterians.
source: The CBM signalosome originated in the ancient ancestor of cnidarians and bilaterians (Staal et al., 2018; Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The overall structure of the CARD of Nematostella vectensis BCL10, predicted with high confidence, is highly similar to that of human BCL10.
source: Using AlphaFold2 (Jumper et al., 2021), we found that the overall structure of the CARD, predicted with high confidence, is highly similar to that of human BCL10, and retains key residues of the polymer interface, such as E53 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is a finding from the AlphaFold2 structural prediction shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–C, supported by a citation.

claim: Nematostella vectensis BCL10 retains key residues of the polymer interface, such as E53.
source: Using AlphaFold2 (Jumper et al., 2021), we found that the overall structure of the CARD, predicted with high confidence, is highly similar to that of human BCL10, and retains key residues of the polymer interface, such as E53 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is a finding from the AlphaFold2 structural prediction shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: The DAmFRET profiles for all three Nematostella vectensis CBM components are strikingly similar to those of their human counterparts.
source: We found that the DAmFRET profiles for all three proteins are strikingly similar to those of their human counterparts.
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiments.

claim: The CARD of Nematostella vectensis CARD-CC polymerized with a high saturating concentration and negligible nucleation barrier.
source: Specifically, the CARD of CARD-CC, the CARD9 homolog, polymerized with a high saturating concentration and negligible nucleation barrier (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Nematostella vectensis BCL10 exhibited a discontinuous, nucleation-limited transition between monomer and polymer.
source: Nv BCL10 exhibited a discontinuous, nucleation-limited transition between monomer and polymer, and the death fold from Nv PCASP1, the MALT1 homolog, remained entirely monomeric (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The death fold from Nematostella vectensis PCASP1, the MALT1 homolog, remained entirely monomeric.
source: Nv BCL10 exhibited a discontinuous, nucleation-limited transition between monomer and polymer, and the death fold from Nv PCASP1, the MALT1 homolog, remained entirely monomeric (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The population of cells with Nematostella vectensis BCL10 polymers also contained activated NF-κB, while cells expressing the same concentration of NvBCL10 in its monomeric form contained inactive NF-κB.
source: By measuring T-Sapphire fluorescence within a DAmFRET experiment, we found that indeed, the population of cells with NvBCL10 polymers also contained activated NF-κB, while cells expressing the same concentration of NvBCL10 in its monomeric form contained inactive NF-κB (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a finding from the DAmFRET experiment shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The function of human BCL10 as a kinetic determinant of cellular decisions has been retained for over 600 million years of animal evolution.
source: Together, these results suggest that the function of human BCL10 as a kinetic determinant of cellular decisions has been retained for over 600 million years of animal evolution.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The all-or-none response of NF-κB has a physical origin in the CBM signalosome.
source: In this study, we investigated the influence of CBM signalosome assembly on the binary kinetics of transcription factor NF-κB activation, a crucial effector of immune signaling. Using biophysical tools and a single-cell reporter of NF-κB activity, we revealed that the all-or-none response of NF-κB has a physical origin in the CBM signalosome, and that it specifically results from an ancient sequence-encoded nucleation barrier in the CARD of the adaptor protein, BCL10.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings in the discussion.

claim: Human CBM mutations that are responsible for pathogen susceptibility and cancer, respectively, increase or decrease the nucleation barrier.
source: Our discovery that human CBM mutations that are responsible for pathogen susceptibility and cancer, respectively, increase or decrease the barrier suggests that it has been evolutionary tuned for optimum immune system function.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings in the discussion.

claim: The nucleation barrier has been evolutionary tuned for optimum immune system function.
source: Our discovery that human CBM mutations that are responsible for pathogen susceptibility and cancer, respectively, increase or decrease the barrier suggests that it has been evolutionary tuned for optimum immune system function.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings in the discussion.

claim: The role of upstream CARD-CC proteins is primarily kinetic in nature and culminates with the initial BCL10-nucleating event.
source: We reiterate that the role of upstream CARD-CC proteins is primarily kinetic in nature and culminates with the initial BCL10-nucleating event, as evidenced by our finding that BCL10 continues to polymerize even after the experimental dissolution of CARD nuclei.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings in the discussion.

claim: Some of the known regulatory modifications to CBM and upstream proteins function to tune the nucleation barrier.
source: We suspect that some of the known regulatory modifications to CBM and upstream proteins function to tune the nucleation barrier.
evidence: This is a speculation in the discussion.

claim: Nucleation barriers large enough to partition identically stimulated cells into discrete states only occur when phase separation is coupled to a conformational transition.
source: We previously showed that nucleation barriers large enough to partition identically stimulated cells into discrete states only occur when phase separation is coupled to a conformational transition (Khan et al., 2018; Posey et al., 2021; Rodríguez Gama et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The preponderance of ordered polymers in immunity signalosomes is consistent with their functioning to confer bistability rather than threshold sensitivity.
source: The preponderance of ordered polymers in immunity signalosomes is therefore consistent with their functioning to confer bistability rather than threshold sensitivity, consistent with the need for immune systems to respond decisively to vastly substoichiometric stimulation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings in the discussion.

claim: Proximity-dependent effector activation does not require any specific polymer structure.
source: This is further evidenced by the fact that (1) proximity-dependent effector activation does not require any specific polymer structure, as shown presently for MALT1 and previously for caspases-1 and -8 (Boucher et al., 2018; Shen et al., 2018; Würstle et al., 2010); and (2) polymers have finite structural nuclei that limit cooperativity (Khan et al., 2018; Vekilov, 2012) whereas phase separation allows for theoretically infinite cooperativity (O'Flynn and Mittag, 2021; Rodríguez Gama et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Signalosome polymers are evolutionary spandrels – byproducts rather than primary targets of natural selection.
source: In our view, signalosome polymers are evolutionary spandrels (Gould and Lewontin, 1979; Manhart and Morozov, 2015) – byproducts rather than primary targets of natural selection.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings in the discussion, supported by citations.

claim: BCL10 function emerges from a kinetic property of its collective that can be conferred by any sufficiently restrictive entropic bottleneck.
source: This is because BCL10 function emerges from a kinetic property of its collective that can be conferred by any sufficiently restrictive entropic bottleneck.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings in the discussion.

claim: That activated BCL10 is an ordered polymer appears to be a consequence of selection for the nucleation barrier more than for some activity of the polymer itself.
source: That activated BCL10 is an ordered polymer appears to be a consequence of selection for that bottleneck more than for some activity of the polymer itself.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings in the discussion.

claim: Extant signalosomes have evolved such a high level of structural order that they do not form spontaneously (or only rarely so) despite a thermodynamic driving force to do so.
source: As opposed to liquid-like non-membrane-bound organelles, extant signalosomes have therefore evolved such a high level of structural order that they do not form spontaneously (or only rarely so) despite a thermodynamic driving force to do so.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings in the discussion.

claim: A protein's structure can evolve via selection for kinetic rather than equilibrium properties of its collective.
source: In short, our results imply that a protein's structure can evolve via selection for kinetic rather than equilibrium properties of its collective.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the findings in the discussion.

claim: That BCL10 and potentially other pro-inflammatory signalosome proteins are constitutively supersaturated implies that cells are thermodynamically predisposed to inflammation.
source: That BCL10 and potentially other pro-inflammatory signalosome proteins are constitutively supersaturated implies that cells are thermodynamically predisposed to inflammation, and therefore hints at an ultimate physical basis for the centrality of inflammation in progressive and age-associated diseases (Furman et al., 2019; López-Otín et al., 2013; Taniguchi and Karin, 2018).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings in the discussion, supported by citations.
